analysis.title: Tin hats and tunnel vision: Equities and higher yields
key_insights: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose from 4.5% at the end of June to around 5.3% at the end of September 2026, making the bond sell-off a defining feature of Q3.
Yields near this level are not unprecedented. They approached it in 2023 and regularly exceeded it before the 2008-2009 Global Financial Crisis.

Equities can keep advancing through rising-yield periods provided earnings remain supportive. Over the past 30 years, sector and industry-group returns tracked changes in earnings expectations in both rising and falling yield regimes.
World earnings expectations grew 29.5% y/y in September, with estimates up 8% during Q3. All 11 sectors in the MSCI World Index recorded y/y growth in earnings expectations.
Semiconductors and semiconductor equipment is a clear outlier, with exceptional increases in both earnings expectations and share prices. Dispersion across groups is considerable.
The authors see the immediate risk as strong fundamentals being extrapolated too far, not equity returns being disconnected from fundamentals.

The margin for error has narrowed. Higher yields raise the return available outside equities, and the market depends heavily on the AI investment cycle (data centres, semiconductors, related infrastructure).
Two distinct risks: earnings expectations may disappoint, or valuations may compress as higher discount rates intensify competition for capital.

The report recommends diversification, valuation discipline and attention to balance-sheet quality rather than abandoning equities. It says defensive equity allocations and disciplined risk control may again prove valuable.

sector_views.rationale: Described as a clear outlier on earnings expectation and share price gains. The report flags dependence on the AI investment cycle as a risk but gives no rating.

earnings_insights: World earnings expectations (MSCI World, forecast basis, not reported results) grew 29.5% y/y in September 2026.
Earnings estimates rose 8% during Q3 2026. All 11 MSCI World sectors recorded y/y growth in earnings expectations.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 4.5% at end of June. Higher yields raise the return available outside equities and increase valuation compression risk.
Starting point for the Q3 sell-off in bonds.
Earnings expectations are strong across all 11 sectors, which has supported equities despite higher yields.

risk_factors: Earnings expectations may disappoint after being extrapolated too far.
Valuations may compress as higher discount rates intensify competition for capital.
A slowdown in AI investment or profitability could challenge current expectations.
Renewed inflation pressures and heightened geopolitical tensions.
charts_described: Figure 3 shows semiconductors and semiconductor equipment as a clear outlier versus the market, with exceptional increases in both earnings expectations and share prices.
vol_and_positioning: The report describes concentrated equity market leadership and market dependence on the AI investment cycle. It gives no volatility or positioning data.
geopolitical: The report cites heightened geopolitical tensions as part of the backdrop, without naming specific events or actors.

tension_points.bull_case: Equities can advance through rising yields while earnings stay supportive. World earnings expectations grew 29.5% y/y in September and all 11 sectors posted growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher yields increase returns outside equities and the market depends on the AI investment cycle. Expectations may disappoint or valuations may compress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An earnings expectation disappointment or a slowdown in AI investment or profitability.
